records.title: CloudFront and the ALB now both wait 60 s, but eCTD compile/assemble still run synchronously and 7 SSE producers plus the MCP transport send no heartbeat, so anything over 60 s is still cut off
records.evidenceAtHead: FIXED half (commit 9cb30bda8, 2026-10-01): terraform/modules/cloudfront/main.tf:186 `origin_read_timeout = 60` on the alb-api custom origin; terraform/modules/alb/main.tf:36 `idle_timeout = 60` (now explicit); server/index.ts:247-248 keepAliveTimeout 65 s / headersTimeout 66 s sit above both. terraform/modules/cloudfront/tests/alb_origin.tftest.hcl:149-164 asserts origin_read_timeout == 60, and terraform-tests.yml runs modules/cloudfront on push (latest run 2026-10-05 success, mocked provider). No test asserts the ALB idle_timeout (terraform/modules/alb/tests has only cloudfront_only.tftest.hcl). The env roots (terraform/environments/{staging,production}/main.tf:42-43) both use ../../stack, so staging gets the same values. OPEN half: (1) Long work is still synchronous in the request. server/routes/ectd-compile.ts:532 POST /:projectIdent/compile assembles the package inline, including PDF/A normalization of every PDF leaf (comment at :1181), and answers only at res.json(result) :1276. server/routes/submission-ops.ts:2345 POST /packages/:packageId/assemble builds leaf PDFs and the zip inline (:2621, :2728, :2974-3091) and answers at :3278. server/routes/submissions.ts:1701 POST /sequences/:seqId/assemble is also inline. server/routes/ectd-export.ts:567 is inline. server/services/docx-pdf-pipeline.ts:14 defaults to 120_000 ms, which is longer than the 60 s edge. No route returns 202 for these; the commit itself says the route half was 'handed on'. The v2 client calls them synchronously: client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/EctdCompile.tsx:1039, GatewayTransmittals.tsx:681, SequenceAssembleTestPackage.tsx:132. (2) SSE heartbeats. 10 server files produce text/event-stream. Three keep the stream alive: ana-ri/stream.ts:845-858 (15 s ': heartbeat'), services/ai-actions/sse-stream.ts:36,114-121 (15 s keepalive, which was already present at 92ccdba1, so the audit's 'only ana-ri' was slightly understated), and contentAssembly.routes.ts:271 (5 s updates). Seven have no heartbeat: ana-features.ts:4948 (submission-chat/stream), ana-intelligence.ts:213 (draft/stream), cortex-unified.ts:526, deep-research.ts:137 (job progress stream), fieldSync.routes.ts:326, ind.ts:372, submissions.ts:1295 (sections/generate). A grep of client/src found no v2 caller for any of the seven; DeepResearch.tsx polls GET /jobs/:id instead. (3) The remote MCP connector: server/mcp/index.ts:174 uses a stateless StreamableHTTPServerTransport, which answers with an SSE stream by default. Its model-backed tools (server/mcp/tools/drafting.ts:27,70; intelligence.ts:14) send no progress notifications and have no timeout (a grep of server/mcp found neither). Durations are still UNVERIFIED: no measured compile or assemble time exists for a pilot-sized package on the production image.
records.remaining: Any request whose response takes more than 60 s still returns a CloudFront 504, and the server keeps going and records the work anyway. 60 s is CloudFront's ceiling without an AWS quota increase. Exposed paths: eCTD compile (inline PDF/A per leaf), package assemble, sequence assemble, eCTD export, and any DOCX→PDF on a route, whose pipeline limit is 120 s. None of these is async yet, so the 504 discards the compile verdict and blockers, which arrive only in the response body. A retry recompiles and records again. The seven SSE producers without a heartbeat are cut after 60 s of silence, but none has a v2 client caller today. MCP drafting/premortem tool calls over 60 s are cut at the edge. The ALB idle_timeout has no test. Real durations have not been measured.
records.severityRationale: The 30–60 s band the audit worried about is closed. What remains sits on the core Submission Center journey (compile and assemble of a real IND, with PDF/A normalization of every leaf inline), so a pilot user who hits a 504 loses the compile verdict, and a retry produces duplicate recorded compilations. Durations are UNVERIFIED. If timing a 50- and 200-leaf package on the production image shows p95 well under 45 s, this drops to P2.
records.humanTestingNote: Local runs have no CloudFront or ALB, so testers will not see this there. On a staging deployment behind CloudFront: in the Submission Center, 'Compile' (eCTD Compile surface), 'Assemble test package' or Gateway package 'Assemble' on a package big enough to take more than 60 s shows a Gateway Timeout or generic request error. The server finishes and records the compile anyway. Workaround: use small packages (a few leaves) when testing on staging. After a timeout, open the compile history (GET /api/ectd-compile/:projectIdent/history, shown on the compile surface) rather than re-running. Log a timeout as 'edge timeout', not as a compile failure. AnA chat is not affected because its stream (ana-ri) sends a heartbeat every 15 s.
records.instructions:
1. Measure before building. Build the production image (Dockerfile.optimized) and run it against a seeded database with Ghostscript and veraPDF present. Time POST /api/ectd-compile/:projectIdent/compile, POST /api/submission-ops/packages/:packageId/assemble, POST /api/submissions/sequences/:seqId/assemble and POST /api/ectd-export/:submissionId for an FDA IND sequence with 50 leaves and with 200 leaves. Record p50 and p95 for each, plus the image digest, under docs/evidence/D1/<date>-edge-timeouts/. If every p95 is under 45 s, record that, skip steps 3-5, and keep steps 2 and 6-8.
2. Pin the ALB half. Add a run to terraform/modules/alb/tests/cloudfront_only.tftest.hcl, or a new alb_timeouts.tftest.hcl, that asserts `aws_lb.this.idle_timeout == 60`. Make it fail first: temporarily set terraform/modules/alb/main.tf:36 to 59, run `terraform test` in terraform/modules/alb, see it fail, restore 60 and see it pass. Add a stack-level assertion that server keepAliveTimeout (server/index.ts:247, 65_000) > ALB idle_timeout. A small vitest in tests/ci/ that reads both files is enough.
3. Make compile asynchronous. Do not create a new job table; reuse the existing tenant-scoped public.artifact_compute_jobs (db/migrations/20260326_artifact_compute_plane.sql:18, already in C2C_MIGRATION_FILES at scripts/db/migration-set.mjs:792; organization_id INTEGER NOT NULL), with surface_key 'ectd-compile' and a runtime_profile_key seeded in that same file's profile INSERT. Any seed change is an in-place amendment with a dated header note (Rule 1). Split server/routes/ectd-compile.ts:532 so the handler validates and resolves the anchor/spine exactly as today. It then inserts the job row with organization_id and the requesting user, starts the existing compileFromSpine/assembly body detached from the response, and returns 202 {jobId}. On finish, the job writes the full CompilationResult (the object built at :1242-1270) into result_summary and sets status 'completed' or 'failed'. A thrown error is stored as status 'failed' with the error and never as an empty result (fail closed). Add GET /api/ectd-compile/:projectIdent/jobs/:jobId. It reads the row filtered by organization_id from the session, never from the request, and returns 404 for a foreign tenant's job.
4. Apply the same 202+poll split to server/routes/submission-ops.ts:2345 (packages/:packageId/assemble) and server/routes/submissions.ts:1701 (sequences/:seqId/assemble, dry run), and to server/routes/ectd-export.ts:567 if step 1 shows it can exceed 45 s. Keep one implementation per capability (Zero duplication): move the existing inline body into a service function that both the job runner and any test call; delete the inline copy.
5. Update the v2 callers to post, then poll every 2 s until a terminal state, showing elapsed time and keeping the existing result rendering: client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/EctdCompile.tsx:1039, GatewayTransmittals.tsx:681 and SequenceAssembleTestPackage.tsx:132. A poll error renders as an error state, never as an empty result. Add a stale-job sweep: a running row older than timeout_seconds becomes 'failed: abandoned (task restarted)'. Run the sweep under the advisory-lock pattern used for background jobs (commit 03dbeaf51) so two API replicas do not both run it.
6. SSE: create one helper, e.g. server/utils/sse-stream.ts openSseStream(req, res). It sets Content-Type text/event-stream, Cache-Control no-cache no-transform, X-Accel-Buffering no; flushes headers; writes ': heartbeat\n\n' every 15 s; clears the interval on req/res 'close'. Use the logic already in server/services/ai-actions/sse-stream.ts:36-142 and server/routes/ana-ri/stream.ts:837-859. Migrate all 10 producers onto it, including those two, and delete their private copies (Zero duplication): ana-features.ts:4948, ana-intelligence.ts:213, contentAssembly.routes.ts:256, cortex-unified.ts:526, deep-research.ts:137, fieldSync.routes.ts:326, ind.ts:372, submissions.ts:1295. If a producer turns out to be unreachable and is deleted instead, the commit must name the replacement path, per the CLAUDE.md working agreement.
7. Add a guard scripts/ci/check-sse-heartbeat.mjs (npm script ci:sse-heartbeat, plus a :selftest). It fails when any server file outside the helper sets text/event-stream. The selftest feeds it a fixture that sets the header directly and asserts exit 1. Wire the guard into ci.yml's lint job and .husky/pre-push next to the other static guards (around line 560).
8. MCP: for tools that can exceed 45 s (server/mcp/tools/drafting.ts c2c_draft_cover_letter and c2c_draft_agency_response; intelligence.ts c2c_run_crl_premortem), send notifications/progress every 15 s when the request carries _meta.progressToken. Give each a 50 s server-side deadline that returns an isError tool result such as 'did not finish within the connector's time limit; continue in the app', never a partial draft presented as complete.
9. Optional, founder/AWS: if step 1 shows the work cannot be made async before the pilot, request the CloudFront 'response timeout per origin' quota increase. Then raise origin_read_timeout and the ALB idle_timeout together, and raise server/index.ts keepAliveTimeout and headersTimeout above both. Update the two tftests.
10. All work lands on concept2cure-v2 directly; merge, never rebase (Rule 0).
records.acceptance: (a) docs/evidence holds measured p50/p95 for compile, package assemble, sequence assemble and export at 50 and 200 leaves on the production image, with the image digest. (b) The new ALB test fails with idle_timeout = 59 and passes with 60; the cloudfront alb_origin test stays green. (c) A route test (vitest, supertest) mocks the assembly service to take 70 s with fake timers and asserts POST /api/ectd-compile/:ident/compile answers 202 with a jobId in under 1 s. This test is written first and seen failing against the current synchronous route (it gets 200 after the mocked delay, or times out). GET .../jobs/:jobId then returns the full CompilationResult with status 'completed'. A second org's session gets 404 for the same jobId. A thrown assembly error yields status 'failed' with the message and never an empty result. (d) The same 202 test passes for submission-ops packages/:packageId/assemble and submissions sequences/:seqId/assemble. (e) ci:sse-heartbeat:selftest exits 1 on the fixture and ci:sse-heartbeat exits 0 on the tree. A vitest on openSseStream with fake timers sees ': heartbeat' written at 15 s and the interval cleared on close. (f) An MCP tool test with a stubbed 70 s model call returns an isError result at the 50 s deadline and emits progress notifications when a progressToken is supplied. (g) On staging behind CloudFront, a 200-leaf compile completes with no 504 in the CloudFront access log.
records.dependencies: OPS-01 (a CloudFront/ALB deployment to measure on), OPS-09 (the production image's document/PDF-A runtime determines real durations), OPS-13 (task sizing affects durations), OPS-07 (job sweep must run once across replicas).

records.title: Nothing still gates landing on concept2cure-v2: the branch is unprotected, the pre-push hook runs no tests, Checkov and schema validation are PR-only, the bot still refreshes the baseline, and trunk CI has not been green since 2026-09-23
records.evidenceAtHead: GitHub API (run 2026-10-13): `gh api repos/concept2cure/ClinicalSageAI-2-replit/branches/concept2cure-v2` → protected=false, required_status_checks enforcement_level 'off'. `.../rulesets` → one ruleset, 11855901 'JMSMITH', enforcement 'disabled', rules deletion and non_fast_forward only. `.../rules/branches/concept2cure-v2` → []. No merge queue is possible without an active ruleset. PR-only workflows have the same triggers as at 92ccdba1: terraform-compliance.yml:3-6 (Checkov, `on: pull_request` paths terraform/**), db-schema-validation.yml:13-18 (drizzle push on an empty DB, pull_request only, and nothing in ci.yml runs drizzle-kit push), test-assembly.yml:3-4, danger.yml, neon-preview-db.yml, pr-checks.yml and ops-audit-plan.yml (PR plus dispatch). pr-checks.yml's gates are all mirrored in ci.yml (checked per script name). Trivy config (ci.yml:2391-2404) does scan IaC on push. .husky/pre-push (707 lines) runs about 35 static guards from line 93 to 697: migration order and drop safety, tenant scope, RLS bypass, SQL interpolation, repo-health ceiling (:587), pushed-file ESLint errors and warnings (:652, :671) and pushed typecheck (:697). It runs no test runner: no vitest, jest or npm test. It is also client-side and bypassable with --no-verify. repo-health-baseline-refresh.yml is unchanged: :17-20 on push to concept2cure-v2, :61-65 commits and pushes the baseline with [skip ci]. `git log --author=github-actions 92ccdba1..HEAD` counts 342 such commits, the latest 696a1d4c8 on 2026-10-13. Partial mitigation added after the audit (f80dc2934): ci.yml:1026-1040 and package.json:363 add audit:repo-health:ceiling, which the bot cannot refresh. It covers oversized files only; other repo-health deltas are still absorbed by the refresh. The nightly-governance job (ci.yml:2459-2558) still ends `exit $failed` over strict gates whose own comment says they are 'EXPECTED to fail', so every scheduled CI run on trunk is red. A post-audit mitigation that gates releases, not landing: deploy-aws.yml:84-143 (ci-verdict, commit 8060c28bc) refuses to deploy a SHA unless ci.yml, semgrep.yml and codeql.yml push runs on it succeeded. Result: `gh api .../actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs?branch=concept2cure-v2&status=success` shows the last green run at 2026-09-23T08:36Z (35838048262). The latest completed push run, 38358525641 (9a59bc8f9, 2026-10-13T06:45Z), failed Lint, Test, Coverage, Integration Tests, Blank DB Provisioning + Deploy Migration ('Deploy migration succeeds on the provisioned database'), Production Boot Smoke ('Provision the schema from scratch') and Production Image Boot; Build and Release evidence were skipped. All 50 completed push runs in the latest 60 failed.
records.remaining: Everything in the audit's fix list is still open: no server-side pre-land gate (branch unprotected, ruleset disabled, no merge queue), no tests before a push lands, Checkov and drizzle schema validation never run on trunk, the bot baseline auto-refresh still absorbs repo-health regressions, and the nightly strict job still turns CI red by design. A new interaction makes this worse: the bot's [skip ci] commits often become the branch tip, and no CI run exists for such a SHA. A v* tag on the tip therefore makes deploy-aws.yml's ci-verdict wait 90 minutes and refuse. Trunk has had no green CI run for about 3 weeks, so no SHA is deployable today.
records.severityRationale: This is not itself a pilot-blocking defect: deploy-aws.yml's ci-verdict now keeps a red SHA out of production. But it is the structural reason trunk stays red (OPS-02, P0). The pilot needs a deployable green SHA that stays green while agents push directly to trunk many times a day. Without a pre-land gate, every fix to OPS-02 is undone by the next push.
records.humanTestingNote: Testers cannot see the missing gate directly, but it decides what they test: a regression can land on trunk between two test builds without anything stopping it. Pin each test environment to one recorded SHA and put that SHA in every bug report. Note that trunk CI currently fails 'Blank DB Provisioning + Deploy Migration' and 'Production Boot Smoke: provision the schema from scratch'. If a fresh test database fails to provision, report it under OPS-02 rather than as a product bug, and reuse an already-provisioned database for that session.
records.instructions:
1. Founder decision first, written into CLAUDE.md. GitHub required status checks, whether through branch protection or a ruleset, refuse a direct push unless the SHA already has green checks from another ref. A merge queue needs PRs. Both conflict with Rule 0 as written. Choose either (A) amend Rule 0 to allow a merge queue into concept2cure-v2 (short-lived queue refs only) and update .husky/pre-push's agent-branch refusal to match, or (B) keep Rule 0 and make the pre-push hook the pre-land test gate (steps 3-4), with server-side protection limited to history (step 2). Do not ship a change that silently contradicts Rule 0.
2. In GitHub settings (founder/admin; the session token gets 403 on branch protection), enable ruleset 11855901, or create a new one, targeting refs/heads/concept2cure-v2 with 'Restrict deletions' and 'Block force pushes'. This is consistent with Rule 0 (merge, never rebase). Under option A, also add the required checks (Lint, Test, Build, Release evidence gate) and enable merge_group, which ci.yml already listens for (ci.yml:8). Verify with `gh api repos/concept2cure/ClinicalSageAI-2-replit/rules/branches/concept2cure-v2` returning non-empty.
3. Under option B, add scripts/ci/check-pushed-tests.mjs, modelled on scripts/ci/check-pushed-lint-errors.mjs. Take the push range from scripts/ci/lib/push-range.mjs (resolvePushBase, changedSince) and run `vitest related --run --config vitest.config.ts <changed files>`, plus `jest --config scripts/jest.config.js --findRelatedTests <changed files>` for jest-owned paths. Fail closed when the runner exits non-zero, crashes, or produces no parseable JSON report. If a change touches more than about 40 source files or a shared core (shared/schema.ts, server/db.ts, server/middleware/**), run a named fast subset instead and say so: test:submission and test:security from package.json:80-83, plus tests/schema-contract. Add `ci:pushed-tests` and `ci:pushed-tests:selftest` to package.json next to ci:pushed-typecheck (package.json:291).
4. Insert the gate into .husky/pre-push after the typecheck block (around :697), using the same refusal pattern ('🚫 ERROR … exit 1'). The selftest must create a temporary source plus spec pair whose spec fails, run the checker against it, and assert exit 1, then assert exit 0 once the spec passes. Show both outcomes in the commit message.
5. Checkov on push: move the Checkov step from terraform-compliance.yml:28-38 into a new job in terraform-tests.yml (already on push to concept2cure-v2 for terraform/**), with soft_fail: false. Delete terraform-compliance.yml in the same change. Its plan step cannot run without AWS credentials, terraform-tests already runs validate, and the PR-comment step is dead under Rule 0. Because Checkov has not run since 2026-06-15, first run it locally (`checkov -d terraform/ --framework terraform`). Put each existing finding in a .checkov.yaml skip list with a written reason per entry, and extend ci:trivyignore-hygiene, or add a sibling guard, so an entry without a reason fails. Prove the job fails by adding a temporary public S3 bucket fixture.
6. Schema validation on push: add `push: branches: [concept2cure-v2]` with the same paths to db-schema-validation.yml:13-18. Prove it fails by temporarily breaking an FK target in a scratch schema file, then revert. For test-assembly.yml, danger.yml, neon-preview-db.yml, pr-checks.yml and ops-audit-plan.yml: either add a push trigger or delete the workflow, naming in the commit message the ci.yml step that already runs each gate. pr-checks.yml's gates are all already in ci.yml.
7. Remove the auto-refresh: delete .github/workflows/repo-health-baseline-refresh.yml. Make docs/reports/repo-health-scan-latest.json a human-maintained ratchet: CI's `audit:repo-health:no-regression` (ci.yml:1023-1025) fails on growth, the pusher either fixes it or updates the baseline in the same commit with a reason, and the pre-push hook runs the same no-regression check next to audit:repo-health:ceiling (:587). This also stops the [skip ci] tip commits that leave deploy-aws.yml's ci-verdict without a run for the tip SHA. Verify by pushing a commit that adds a duplicate basename and seeing pre-push refuse it.
8. Nightly strict: move the nightly-governance job (ci.yml:2459-2558) into its own workflow file (e.g. governance-nightly.yml, schedule plus dispatch). Its expected failures then stop marking the CI workflow red on trunk, and it keeps its counts and artifact upload.
9. Land on concept2cure-v2 only, merging and never rebasing. These gates only make sense once trunk is green, so do OPS-02 first or in the same window.
records.acceptance: (a) `gh api repos/concept2cure/ClinicalSageAI-2-replit/rules/branches/concept2cure-v2` lists non_fast_forward and deletion rules, and under option A also required status checks plus a merge queue. A force-push to concept2cure-v2 is refused by GitHub. (b) ci:pushed-tests:selftest exits 1 on its failing fixture and 0 on its passing one. A real push whose change breaks a related vitest is refused by .husky/pre-push, as demonstrated in the commit message, and a docs-only push skips the test step and says so. (c) Checkov runs on a push touching terraform/** and fails on the public-bucket fixture; terraform-compliance.yml no longer exists, and .checkov.yaml has no entry without a reason (its guard fails when one is added). (d) db-schema-validation runs on a push to concept2cure-v2 touching shared/schema.ts. (e) repo-health-baseline-refresh.yml is gone and `git log --author=github-actions` gains no new commits after the change. A push adding a duplicate basename is refused pre-push. (f) Scheduled runs no longer appear as failures of the 'CI' workflow. (g) After OPS-02, ten consecutive push runs of ci.yml on concept2cure-v2 are green, and a v* tag on the tip SHA passes deploy-aws.yml's ci-verdict job.
records.dependencies: OPS-02 (trunk must be green before required checks or a pre-push test gate are usable). Founder decision on Rule 0 versus a merge queue (step 1). GitHub admin access for the ruleset (step 2).
